scripts._comment_lint_globs: One character separates these globs from each other: `packages/*/src` is one directory level, `packages/**/src` is any, and the difference is exactly the 33 files under `packages/examples/*/src` that prettier always checked and eslint never did. What NEITHER covers, so no lint or format gate here sees it: `packages/*/tests/**`, every `tsup.config.ts`, `scripts/*.mjs`, and the root configs. Widen deliberately, not by accident.
scripts._comment_release_check_graph: FIVE gates in this repository have been found written and invoked by nothing — test:packed asserting a deleted API, check-bundle-size wired into nothing, prettier rewriting benchmark markup, graph:check, and graph:verify. The pattern is not bad luck: a gate that is written but never invoked looks identical, in a diff, to one that runs. That is what check:gates now guards. ORDER: graph:check and graph:verify run before typecheck because they need nothing built and are the cheapest steps in the chain that can fail. History: docs-site/docs/architecture/gates-and-root-configs.md
scripts.release:check: npm run build:all && npm run check:src-emit && npm run check:doc-pointers && npm run check:json-render-links-no-compiler && npm run check:plugin-prices && npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run graph:check && npm run graph:verify && npm run check:computed-shake && npm run check:assert-shake && npm run check:example-pages && npm run atlas:verify && npm run check:gates && npm run typecheck && npm run typecheck:tests && npm run typecheck:benchmarks && npm run test:types && npm run check:docs && npm run check:doc-examples && npm run check:citations && npm run check:llms && npm run check:size && npm run check:minimal-page && npm run check:numbers && npm run build:wasm && npm run test:run && npm run test:react-libraries
scripts.release: npm run release:check && npm run test:packed && npm run publish:all
scripts.release:dry: npm run release:check && npm run publish:dry
scripts._comment_typecheck: THE GATE FORCES, THE INNER LOOP DOES NOT. `tsc -b` reuses `.tsbuild` state and decides what to recheck from timestamps, so after a rename or a branch switch it reports zero errors over a tree whose imports are broken — 52 test files failed to load while the compiler said nothing. A fresh CI clone cannot hit it; a working copy hits it constantly. So `typecheck` is the honest command and `typecheck:incremental` is the fast one you reach for deliberately.
scripts._comment_typecheck_benchmarks: SEPARATE FROM THE BUILD GRAPH ON PURPOSE, and in the gate anyway. `packages/benchmarks` cannot join `tsconfig.build.json`: it compiles competitors, and Solid's jsxImportSource, an Angular app and a Marko one each want options that contradict that graph's. Its own `tsconfig.typecheck.json` excludes the competitor participants and checks everything else, so a new axis is covered by default and a new unclassified participant fails loudly.
scripts._comment_typecheck_tests: Runs one `tsconfig.tests.json` per package, each extending that package's OWN typecheck config so a test resolves @exodra/core to the identical .d.ts its sources do. A single root project with a wildcard `@exodra/*` map does NOT work — it produces type doppelgangers. It sits immediately after `npm run typecheck` in the chain because the `paths` it inherits name `.tsbuild`, which that step is what produces. Why the build graph excludes test files at all, and what arming this gate found: docs-site/docs/architecture/gates-and-root-configs.md
scripts._comment_pretest: THE SUITE REFUSES TO RUN ON A CONTAMINATED TREE. npm runs `pre<name>` before `<name>`, so these three hooks put check:src-emit in front of every entry point that reports a test result — a stray `.js` beside a `.ts` is loaded IN PREFERENCE to it, making the run green or red about code nobody is looking at. `npx vitest` typed directly still bypasses this: the hook is npm's, not vitest's.
scripts.build:wasm: export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"; command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo '❌ build:wasm: cargo is not on PATH, and it is not in $HOME/.cargo/bin either. The SWC plugin is compiled from Rust to WebAssembly. Install rustup: https://rustup.rs'; exit 1; }; command -v rustup >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo '❌ build:wasm: cargo was found but rustup was not, in $HOME/.cargo/bin or on PATH. The installed-target list belongs to rustup; a cargo installed on its own (Homebrew does this) cannot answer for it. Install rustup: https://rustup.rs'; exit 1; }; rustup target list --installed | grep -q wasm32-wasip1 || { echo '❌ build:wasm: rustup is installed but the wasm32-wasip1 target is not. Run: rustup target add wasm32-wasip1'; exit 1; }; npm run build --workspace=swc-plugin-exodra
scripts._comment_check_computed_shake: Asks the question check:size structurally cannot: not `is this package too big` but `which page pays for which subsystem`. It bundles two fixture pages against packages/core/src and asserts, from esbuild's metafile rather than by grepping minified output, that no module of the computed system reaches the page that never composes it. A module reaching that page and named in neither table in the script is reported UNCLASSIFIED rather than passed.
scripts._comment_check_example_pages: An example page is the only Exodra code nothing else compiles, lints or runs — it is plain HTML loading dist/ by import map, so a renamed door rots it silently and the symptom is a blank screen with nothing in the console. This reads the door list out of EXO_DOM_NODE_VOCABULARY.ts rather than keeping its own, refuses any `c.<door>(` the vocabulary does not have, and refuses an import of a name the named package does not export. WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, and what cost this page months of being dead: a bare specifier missing from the IMPORT MAP. The names were all real; @exodra/core's dist imports @exodra/context, the map did not list it, and the whole module graph failed to link before one line ran.
scripts._comment_check_numbers: Sits AFTER build:all, beside check:size, and not with the other docs gates: its size half gzips files in dist/, so before the build it would either brick a clean checkout or skip itself silently — and a gate whose half no-ops is the failure mode three gates here were found to have. The docs half needs nothing built, so `npm run check:numbers` alone still checks every table.
scripts._comment_check_src_emit: The gate against a suite that lies: a compiled .js beside a .ts is resolved in preference to it, so vitest silently runs stale copies and every number taken off such a tree is worthless while nothing goes red. It runs SECOND in release:check, before lint, because `prebuild` sweeps the strays away at build:all and takes the evidence with them. What produced 650 such files, and why `git status` stayed clean through it: docs-site/docs/architecture/gates-and-root-configs.md
scripts._comment_check_json_render: Shipping schemas instead of declarations pays off only if the page never LINKS the compiler, which is an import-graph fact and invisible to every test: the two paths agree precisely because the compiler is still there to be compared against. This walks the graph from the two entries a build-compiled page uses.
